title: W_COVER measured for the first time: what the model can actually produce
the_question: 'you sure this is the smartest approach?' (ninth time)
the_answer: no reframing this round. The binding quantity named in r97 -- W_COVER, positive professional task coverage -- is measured for the first time.
instrument: unified model, digest 908bedbb, 443 capabilities; executed through verified_bound_capability_execution_adapter_v1 (re-reads the live registry, re-renders the frozen template, re-verifies the trace). No external model, no network. r90 gate: PASSES.

routing_layer_result.test: route a professional-production goal to a capability
routing_layer_result.reading: ROUTING WORKS. It was never the bottleneck. r93's diagnosis holds and now has a clean confirmation on a second task family.

detail.xlsx.table.create_from_json_records: PASS -- 5333-byte valid OOXML workbook, 10 parts, shared strings ['region','revenue','units','Qena','Cairo'] -- real data, real file, verified by an independent reader
detail.python.tests.generate.scaffold.v1: CRASH (prints JSON and exits instead of raising)

the_structurally_important_finding.pdf_capabilities_in_model: 3, and all 3 are EXTRACTORS (read a pdf), ZERO producers (make a pdf)
the_structurally_important_finding.consequence: the single most common GDPval deliverable -- pdf, 85 of 220 -- has NO producer in a 443-capability model. W_COVER is bounded above by the producer set, not by routing, not by intelligence. A perfect router over 443 capabilities still cannot emit a pdf.

the_w_cover_number.definition: share of GDPval deliverable extensions for which the model holds at least one RUNNABLE and CORRECT producer
the_w_cover_number.by_row_frequency: xlsx 65/220 = 29.5% of tasks have a producer; pdf 85/220 = 0%; docx 64/220 present but producer FAIL_CLOSED on the declared contract
the_w_cover_number.honest_statement: on the best reading, W_COVER_STRUCTURAL <= 29.5%; on the strict reading (only producers that actually executed), 1 of 220 deliverable families is demonstrated end-to-end
the_w_cover_number.whole_task_semantic_membership_from_the_: 0 of 220 (pre-existing artifact, unchanged by this round)

what_is_real: a 443-capability zero-weight model routed a real professional goal correctly and emitted a genuine, independently-validated Excel workbook from structured data. That had never been done in this project before this round.
what_is_not_real: that constitutes GDPval capability. GDPval-AA compares complete submissions against a frozen Opus 5.5 reference at elo 1846, with ~47 rubric items per task. Three successful file writers are not a submission.

the_binding_constraint_named_for_the_fir.not_weights: the model has none and does not need any to write an xlsx
the_binding_constraint_named_for_the_fir.it_is_SUPPLY: the model holds producers for 1 of the 4 deliverable families GDPval asks for, and 0 producers for the most common one. Capability coverage, not capability quality, is the ceiling.
the_binding_constraint_named_for_the_fir.implication: the correct next build is not a better router or a better agent. It is PRODUCERS -- pdf first (85 tasks), then repair docx and sqlite to honour their own declared contracts.

runner_side_defects_found.solve_reroutes: UnifiedModel.solve(goal, inputs) routes the goal text again, so a goal that names the effect rather than the capability can be silently diverted; my first sweep had 0/12 for exactly this reason
runner_side_defects_found.input_name_mismatch: the declared input contract differs per capability (spec vs content, json_path vs records); a caller cannot infer it
runner_side_defects_found.crash_instead_of_raise: python.tests.generate.scaffold.v1 prints JSON and exits rather than raising, so a programmatic caller sees a crash
runner_side_defects_found.registry_lacks_libraries: docx.document.create.python_docx fails on BOUND_APT_METADATA_NOT_FOUND:python3-docx even though the library is installed -- the binding is to apt metadata, not to the import
